title: Can the last grid be filled in more than one way?
description: The last grid has a border sum and only two tiles filled. The video finds the tiles that may be chosen freely and builds two different fillings from two different choices. Both are checked by adding the four sides.
teaching_notes: One idea: when a grid leaves tiles free, a different free choice gives a different filling, and every filling still reaches the border sum. Watch for students who believe a fixed border sum allows only one filling.

video_script.why: The child fills the last grid in two different ways and sees that free tiles allow more than one filling.
video_script.substitution: The book's own last grid with 7 and -5 given, and the book's filling as the first way.
video_script.anchor: a square of nine tiles from the book, with the middle tile missing
video_script.payoff_line: Different free choices give different fillings, and every filling reaches the border sum.

final_answer.value: Several ways; for example top row 7, -2, -9; middle row -3, empty, -5; bottom row -8, -6, 10, or top row 7, -3, -8; middle row -3, empty, -5; bottom row -8, -5, 9.
final_answer.spoken: there are several ways, and two of them are shown on the board

hold_back: Several ways; for example top row 7, -2, -9; middle row -3, empty, -5; bottom row -8, -6, 10, or top row 7, -3, -8; middle row -3, empty, -5; bottom row -8, -5, 9.
maths_rules: border sum is -4; given 7 top left and -5 middle right
free choices: the top right tile and the middle left tile; the other tiles then follow from the sides

first way (the book's): top right -9, top middle -2, bottom right 10, middle left -3, bottom left -8, bottom middle -6; top row 7 + (-2) + (-9) = -4; bottom row -8 + (-6) + 10 = -4; left column 7 + (-3) + (-8) = -4; right column -9 + (-5) + 10 = -4

second way: top right -8, top middle -3, bottom right 9, middle left -3, bottom left -8, bottom middle -5; top row 7 + (-3) + (-8) = -4; bottom row -8 + (-5) + 9 = -4; left column 7 + (-3) + (-8) = -4; right column -8 + (-5) + 9 = -4
a different free choice gives a different filling, and the book also invites other ways
video_script.design: The last grid shown twice side by side. The free tiles are circled, and each filling is built by lighting a side and showing the move up or down on the number line.
open_questions: The book says several ways work, so the video shows the book's filling and one more, and does not claim these are the only two.

narration: <bookmark mark='move'/>A plus number moves us up the number line. A minus number moves us down.
<bookmark mark='name'/>All four sides of a grid add up to one number.
That number is called the border sum.
<bookmark mark='need'/>To fill an empty tile, add the known numbers, then find the move to the border sum.

narration: <bookmark mark='choose'/>Step two, the first way. Choose negative nine for the top right tile and negative three for the middle left tile.
<bookmark mark='top'/>Seven plus negative nine is negative two, so move down two.
The top middle tile is negative two.
<bookmark mark='right'/>Negative nine plus negative five is negative fourteen, so move up ten.

<bookmark mark='left'/>Seven plus negative three is four, so move down eight.

<bookmark mark='bottom'/>Negative eight plus ten is two, so move down six.

<bookmark mark='bottom'/>The bottom left tile stays negative eight.
